text: Capturing light through a lens is a form of art, involving the exposure of a visual image. Two key settings control this process: shutter speed and aperture. Shutter speed refers to the length of time the camera's sensor is exposed to light, while aperture is the opening in the lens that controls the amount of light entering. These two elements work together to determine the overall brightness and depth of the image. Adjusting the shutter speed and aperture allows photographers to create a wide range of effects, from fast-paced action shots to dramatic landscapes.
